expectations.note: Band 1 over the authored closed-horizon population, one direction and one control set, never pooled with the other. The loose and tight sets draw different names, so the two panels can disagree; a population whose tight set was its loose set would be blind to the defect 3.3 found by hand. The captured fixture holds one market day, so no horizon closes in it, forward.written is legitimately nought and every band 1 panel is withheld. That is how ForwardReturnFiller binding its subject kind to the literal "setup" survived twelve checkpoints: nothing ran the query that came back empty against a store with anything to put in it. This population is authored, deterministic, and kept in a store of its own so none of its counts is ever added to a captured one. AUTHORED input: 24 nights, 6 setups a night on each side, 5 controls per set per setup, bars from splitmix64 at a published seed.

expectations.producedBy: an independent restatement of the population's own stated shape, computed outside the solution by tools/derive-indicators.py --accumulation
expectations.note: The session count each band 1 panel was built over, and the floor it is read against. Checkpoint 3.6 fires on at least twenty sessions AND at least 262 effective observations, and the two are needed because they are settled by different things: sessions are what the block bootstrap needs before an interval exists at all, observations are what the decision needs before the interval means anything. This figure reached neither the store nor the screen until migration 034. PairedInterval.Estimate has carried it since the interval was written, ScoreboardBuilder read five of its six fields, the scoreboard table had no column for it, and the panel rendered the row count and the effective count; the session count appeared only inside withheld_because, in prose, and that column is null the moment an interval exists. So the panel could not tell twenty sessions from two hundred at exactly the point the difference starts to matter. Restated rather than read back: every setup in this population has all four horizons written, so every authored night closes and contributes exactly one night to the difference series, which is a different claim from accumulation.nights. AUTHORED input: 24 nights, 6 setups a night on each side, 5 controls per set per setup, bars from splitmix64 at a published seed.

That is how ForwardReturnFiller binding its subject kind to the literal "setup" survived twelve checkpoints: nothing ran the query that came back empty against a store with anything to put in it. This population is authored, deterministic, and kept in a store of its own so none of its counts is ever added to a captured one. AUTHORED input: 24 nights, 6 setups a night on each side, 5 controls per set per setup, bars from splitmix64 at a published seed.

expectations.producedBy: the same population with every control outcome deleted, rebuilt, so the words come from the stage rather than from a stub
expectations.note: The exact state the defect produced: every setup outcome closed and no control outcome at all. The panel said "no session has a closed 10-session horizon yet" while thirty nights of closed horizons sat in the store, which sent a reader to wait for something that had already happened. Frozen as the words rather than as a count, because the words are the whole of what a person had to diagnose it from. **The long side against the loose set, and the id says so**: the reason is measured per direction and per control set, so a figure naming neither would be one of four. surface-claims holds that the page does not swallow the words; this holds that the stage says them.

expectations.note: the authored setup row's own verdict for this gate, reported beside the detectors' counts and never added to them. The row bypasses the recording floor, which is why it carries `uptrend` failed on a grade of `mixed`. expectations.note: Was 2. Moved at 3.0(e), which took the harness's own authored setup row out of the detectors' counters. The row arrives through the store like any other and was counted beside two rows a detector wrote, so every long count carried it. The gate cases were already kept out and said so; this row was not, which is the same rule with one of its subjects missing. The figure now counts detector-written rows only, and the authored row is reported beside it under authoredRow.

expectations.producedBy: an independent resolution of the same IANA identifier through CPython's zoneinfo, computed outside the solution by tools/derive-indicators.py --session
expectations.note: Checkpoint 1.2's figure, being the clock abstraction resolving an IANA identifier rather than a fixed offset. The last instant of 2026-08-24 in America/New_York, in UTC. The two implementations read the same tzdata by different code paths in different runtimes, which is what the tier claims and all it claims: it cannot catch tzdata itself being wrong, and it does catch the lookup failing or silently answering in UTC. That last one is the case worth having, because it is what InvariantGlobalization does and CLAUDE.md names it as the setting that silently breaks IANA lookup. The date is inside daylight saving, so the offset is -4 and a build that had fallen back to UTC would read 2026-08-24T23:59:59Z here.

expectations.note: the best match's distance on each dimension separately, never blended. A single number cannot say which dimension a match was bad on, which is what a reader needs when a comparison looks surprising. Two keys were added to every match_quality on 2026-08-30 when the tight set was allowed to reach across sessions: `marketMood`, which reads "same" on the tight set and "not matched" on the loose one, and `sessionsApart`, which records how far the draw reached. The reach was reversed on 2026-08-31 and both keys stay (see: The tight control set draws within the night, because a within-night draw controls the market mood exactly). `sessionsApart` is nought on every row of every set now, and it was nought here before the reversal too, because the golden fixture holds one market day and the only session a tight draw could reach was the setup's own. So this expectation held the recorded shape rather than the reach and is unmoved by the reversal. What it now asserts is the invariant rather than a coincidence of the fixture. ControlMatchingTests and ControlSamplerTests over authored multi-session stores, which is where it can be exercised at all.

expectations.producedBy: an independent restatement of the nearest-neighbour draw over the fixture's own indicator rows, computed outside the solution by tools/derive-indicators.py --controls
expectations.note: the best match's distance on each dimension separately, never blended. A single number cannot say which dimension a match was bad on, which is what a reader needs when a comparison looks surprising. Two keys were added to every match_quality on 2026-08-30 when the tight set was allowed to reach across sessions: `marketMood`, which reads "same" on the tight set and "not matched" on the loose one, and `sessionsApart`, which records how far the draw reached. The reach was reversed on 2026-08-31 and both keys stay (see: The tight control set draws within the night, because a within-night draw controls the market mood exactly). `sessionsApart` is nought on every row of every set now, and it was nought here before the reversal too, because the golden fixture holds one market day and the only session a tight draw could reach was the setup's own. So this expectation held the recorded shape rather than the reach and is unmoved by the reversal. What it now asserts is the invariant rather than a coincidence of the fixture. ControlMatchingTests and ControlSamplerTests over authored multi-session stores, which is where it can be exercised at all.

an independent restatement of the studentised moving-block bootstrap and the variance-inflation and design-effect discounts in tools/derive-indicators.py --interval, agreeing with the shipped code to every place printed over a series whose nights differ in pair count, which is the population the even scenarios could not reach
expectations.note: Eighty pairs a night whose nightly means vary by exactly what within-night independence predicts. The pairing has removed the market factor, so the night is worth its own pairs and the effective sample should be close to the row count rather than to the night count. Without a case of this shape the row count is never credited and the measurement collapses to the pessimistic corner on every series. AUTHORED input: mean 0.004, uniform wobble +/-0.0193649 being exactly within/sqrt(pairs) rescaled for a uniform, 80 pairs a night at a within-night dispersion of 0.1, seed 5, 40 nights.
